Question_text: In this experiment, you will investigate the time taken for a mass to rotate on the end of a wire. You are provided with • a stopwatch, • a length of wire, • a 100g mass hanger with a pointer, • seven 100 g slotted masses, • safety glasses, • a stand, boss and clamp to hold the wire and mass set. The Supervisor has set up the apparatus as shown in Fig. 1.1 with all seven slotted masses on the mass hanger. You must wear the safety glasses throughout this experiment.
image: Fig. 1.1 shows a side view of the experimental setup. A vertical stand, boss, and clamp are used to hold a wire at the top. The wire hangs down, and at its lower end, a mass hanger with multiple slotted masses is attached. A pointer extends horizontally from the mass hanger. The components are labeled: 'stand, boss and clamp', 'wire', 'slotted masses and mass hanger', and 'pointer'.

Parts.part_text: Observe the position of the pointer when the mass is at rest. By pushing against the end of the pointer, rotate the mass through two complete revolutions in a clockwise direction as shown in Fig. 1.2. When released the mass rotates in an anticlockwise direction until it stops for the first time. It then rotates in a clockwise direction. Determine an accurate time t₁ for the mass to rotate from this initial position until it stops for the first time.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.2 shows a top-down view of the circular mass with a pointer. A dashed circle indicates the path of the pointer's movement. An arrow indicates a clockwise rotation from the 'rest position of pointer', illustrating the initial rotation before release.

Parts.part_text: Remove six slotted masses from the mass hanger. Repeat (a) to determine the new time t₂.

Question_text: In this experiment, you will investigate the width of a shadow. You are provided with • a lamp in a lamp holder connected to a power supply, • an opaque cylindrical object, • a 30 cm ruler.

Parts.part_text: Place the lamp holder on Fig. 2.1 on page 5 so that the centre of the filament of the lamp is directly above the point labelled X. Place the cylinder upright on Fig. 2.1 so that its centre is on the point labelled Y. With the lamp switched on, there is a shadow of the cylinder on Fig. 2.1. Determine the length L_s of the shadow along the line PZQ.
Parts.image: Fig. 2.1 shows a diagram with a vertical dashed line. Point X is located at the top of this line, and point Y is located further down on the same line. A horizontal line, labelled P at the left end, Z in the middle (intersecting the vertical dashed line), and Q at the right end, represents the surface where the shadow is cast.

Parts.part_text: Describe how you could investigate the relationship between the cylinder's position along the line XYZ and the length of the shadow along PZQ.
On Fig. 2.2, sketch a graph of the relationship between the cylinder's position along the line XYZ and the length of the shadow along PZQ.
Parts.image: Fig. 2.2 shows a graph template. The x-axis is labelled 'position of cylinder' with points X, Y, and Z indicated along it. The y-axis is unlabelled but implicitly represents the 'length of shadow'.

Question_text: In this experiment, you will investigate an electrical circuit containing a light-emitting diode (LED). You are provided with • a power supply, • a switch, • a 330 Ω resistor, • a light-emitting diode (LED).

Parts.part_text: The Supervisor has set up the circuit as shown in Fig. 3.1. You are also provided with a voltmeter with two connecting leads that may be connected between various points in the circuit. Connect the voltmeter across the 330 Ω resistor between points A and B. Ensure that the positive (+) terminal of the voltmeter is connected to A. Close the switch. Record the voltmeter reading V_AB.
Parts.image: Fig. 3.1 shows an electrical circuit diagram. A d.c. power supply, indicated by a long and short parallel line with '+' and '-' labels, is connected in series with a switch. Following the switch, there is a 330 Ω resistor, with terminals labeled A and B. Immediately after the resistor, a light-emitting diode (LED) is connected, with terminals labeled B and C. The circuit forms a closed loop.

Parts.part_text: Open the switch. Disconnect the voltmeter from points A and B. Connect the voltmeter across the LED between points B and C. Ensure that the positive (+) terminal of the voltmeter is connected to B. Close the switch. Record the voltmeter reading V_BC.

Open the switch. Disconnect the voltmeter from points B and C. Connect the voltmeter between points A and C. Ensure that the positive (+) terminal of the voltmeter is connected to A. Close the switch. Record the voltmeter reading V_AC. Open the switch.
The current I in the circuit is given by I = V_AB / R where R = 330Ω. Calculate I.
Calculate the resistance R_L of the LED using R_L = V_BC / I.

Question_text: In this experiment, you will investigate the rate of temperature increase of a coil of wire. You are provided with • a cell, • a switch, • an ammeter, • a thermometer, • a length of coiled wire, • connecting leads, • a stopwatch.

Parts.part_text: The Supervisor has set up a circuit as shown in Fig. 4.1. It shows a wire coiled around the end of a thermometer. The switch is open. Record the temperature θ of the thermometer at room temperature.
Parts.image: Fig. 4.1 shows an electrical circuit diagram connected to a thermal setup. A cell is connected in series with a switch and an ammeter (labeled 'A'). The circuit then goes through a coiled wire, which is wrapped around the bulb of a thermometer. The switch is depicted in an open state.

Parts.part_text: Close the switch and record the ammeter reading I after 5 seconds. Immediately open the switch.
Calculate the power P supplied to the coil using P = I²R where the resistance R, of the coil, is 4.0Ω.

You will record the reading on the stopwatch when the thermometer reaches certain temperatures. You will start the stopwatch when the thermometer reaches 2.0°C more than your value for θ in (a). Write headings in the top row of the results table of Fig. 4.2. Close the switch. Start the stopwatch when the temperature is θ_r + 2.0°C. For each further 2.0°C rise in temperature record the time shown on the stopwatch. Continue to record times until the temperature has risen by 18.0°C. Open the switch. Record all of your results in the table of Fig. 4.2. Include the temperature reading when you started the stopwatch.
Parts.image: Fig. 4.2 displays an empty table with multiple rows and two columns, designed for recording experimental results, specifically temperature and corresponding time readings.

Parts.part_text: Using the grid opposite, plot a graph of time on the y-axis against temperature on the x-axis.
Determine the gradient of your graph when the temperature is θ_r + 11°C.
